text: Alex Morgan. Senior software engineer with nine years' experience in distributed systems and payments infrastructure. Employment: Lead engineer at Northgate Fintech, 2021 to present, owning the settlement pipeline and a team of six. Software engineer at Blue River Analytics, 2017 to 2021, building streaming ingestion in Java and Kafka. Education: BSc Computer Science, University of Leeds, first class. Skills: Go, Java, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Terraform, incident response. Interests: hill walking, chess, home brewing. References available on request.

Weekly planning, Tuesday. Attendees: Priya, Tom, Sam. Sprint review moved to Thursday because the demo environment is being rebuilt. Tom to finish the invoice export by Friday and chase the vendor about the API rate limit. Priya raised the onboarding document being out of date; Sam will own the rewrite. Budget for the offsite approved at last week's figure. Next meeting same time; Sam to circulate the agenda by Monday.

Lemon drizzle loaf. Cream 225 g softened butter with 225 g caster sugar until pale. Beat in four eggs one at a time, then fold in 225 g self-raising flour and the zest of two lemons. Bake in a lined loaf tin at 180 degrees for 45 to 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. While warm, prick the top and pour over the juice of the lemons mixed with 85 g granulated sugar. Leave in the tin to cool completely before slicing.

Version 4.2.1. Fixed a race in the connection pool that could leak sockets under retry storms. The exporter now streams rows instead of buffering the whole result set. Config keys renamed: timeout_ms becomes request_timeout; the old key is accepted with a deprecation warning until 5.0. Dropped support for Python 3.8. Known issue: the Windows installer still requires a reboot after upgrading the service.

A band of rain crosses the north west this morning, clearing eastwards by early afternoon with brighter spells following. Highs of 17 in the south, 13 further north with a fresh westerly breeze on exposed coasts. Overnight lows around 8 with patchy mist in sheltered valleys. Tomorrow drier and warmer, with the risk of an isolated shower over high ground later.

A late header settled a scrappy derby that produced few chances until the final quarter of an hour. The visitors dominated possession without troubling the goalkeeper, and the home side's counter-attacks kept breaking down at the edge of the box. The winner came from a corner in the 87th minute after the defence failed to clear. Both managers spoke of tired legs after the midweek fixtures.

45-year-old right-handed man with six weeks of pain over the lateral aspect of the right elbow, worse when gripping and lifting a kettle, after taking up racquet sports again. Point tenderness over the lateral epicondyle, pain on resisted wrist extension, full range of movement, no swelling or redness, neurovascularly intact. Impression: lateral epicondylitis. Plan: activity modification, a counterforce brace, simple analgesia, eccentric loading exercises; review in six weeks.

19-year-old man with two weeks of pain and redness along the medial edge of the right big toenail after cutting the nail short. Nail fold swollen and tender with a small amount of granulation tissue, no discharge, no spreading redness, afebrile. Impression: ingrowing toenail. Plan: warm salt-water soaks twice daily, cotton wool under the nail edge, roomier footwear, cut the nail straight across; podiatry referral if it recurs.

32-year-old woman asks for advice before a two-week sailing holiday. Lifelong motion sickness in cars and boats, with nausea and cold sweats within twenty minutes of setting off, settling within an hour of stopping. Otherwise well, no medications, not pregnant. Plan: hyoscine patch or cinnarizine before travel, sit facing forward with a view of the horizon, avoid reading below deck.

27-year-old man with itchy, scaling skin between the fourth and fifth toes of both feet for three weeks, worse after the gym. Macerated white skin in the web spaces with fissuring, no nail changes, no spread to the soles. Impression: tinea pedis. Plan: topical terbinafine for one to two weeks after the rash clears, dry between the toes, alternate shoes, flip-flops in communal showers.

38-year-old man with flaking, mildly itchy scalp for several months, worse in winter, with some greasy scale at the hairline and eyebrows. No hair loss, no redness beyond the scalp, no nail changes. Impression: seborrhoeic dermatitis of the scalp. Plan: ketoconazole shampoo twice weekly for four weeks then as needed; a mild topical steroid scalp application for a week if itch persists.

58-year-old man with three nosebleeds in the past fortnight, each from the left nostril, lasting ten to fifteen minutes and stopping with pressure. No anticoagulants, no bleeding elsewhere, no bruising, blood pressure 128 over 82 today. Anterior rhinoscopy shows a prominent vessel on the left septum. Plan: naseptin cream twice daily for two weeks; first-aid advice on pinching the soft part of the nose leaning forward; ENT referral for cautery if it recurs.

49-year-old woman with four months of heel pain, worst with the first steps in the morning and after sitting, improving with walking. Works standing all day, recently gained weight. Tender at the medial calcaneal tubercle, tight calves, no swelling, no numbness. Impression: plantar fasciitis. Plan: calf and plantar fascia stretches, supportive footwear, weight advice, simple analgesia; physiotherapy if no better in three months.

24-year-old woman with itchy, purple-red swellings on the toes of both feet each winter for the past three years, appearing a few hours after coming in from the cold and lasting one to two weeks. No ulceration, no history of Raynaud's, no joint symptoms, otherwise well. Impression: chilblains. Plan: keep the feet warm and dry, avoid rapid rewarming, warm socks and footwear; no medication needed.

41-year-old man returning from Sydney for a two-week work trip asks how to manage jet lag; on previous trips he has slept poorly for a week and felt foggy in meetings. Otherwise well, no medications. Plan: shift sleep an hour a day before departure, bright light in the destination morning, avoid caffeine after midday and alcohol on the flight, short daytime naps only in the first two days.

29-year-old woman with a painless, firm, pea-sized lump on the back of the right wrist for two months, more prominent with wrist flexion, occasionally aching after typing. Smooth, transilluminates, not fixed to skin, no neurological symptoms. Impression: ganglion cyst. Plan: reassurance; no treatment unless it becomes painful or limits function, in which case aspiration or surgical referral.

36-year-old man with intermittent hiccups over the past two days, each bout lasting up to twenty minutes and settling on its own, no vomiting, no chest pain, no swallowing difficulty, eating and drinking normally. Started after a large meal and several beers. Impression: benign self-limiting hiccups. Plan: reassurance; smaller meals, avoid carbonated drinks; return if bouts last over 48 hours or new symptoms appear.

22-year-old woman with a tender red lump on the edge of the right upper eyelid for three days, mild watering, vision normal, no redness of the eye itself, no fever. Small pointing swelling at a lash follicle. Impression: external hordeolum. Plan: warm compresses several times a day, lid hygiene, avoid eye make-up until settled; return if the swelling spreads or vision changes.
